assumptions: USD million; fictional Hazel Market. All figures final FY2025 unless dated otherwise. Net merchandise sales exclude taxes and returns. Third-party marketplace commission is net revenue; GMV is a transaction metric.

evidence.text: [FY2024] Own-store net sales400, own-online net sales160; marketplace GMV200, commission24. Total recognized revenue584. EBITDA45. Marketplace was agent throughout.

[FY2025 commerce note] Own-store gross checkout500 includes VAT40 and customer returns20 excluding VAT; net sales440. Own-online net sales210. Third-party marketplace GMV300 excludes VAT/returns, commission36. No other revenue.
[Costs] Own-store COGS280, own-online COGS135; store selling costs90, online fulfillment35, marketplace operating costs18, corporate cash-type expense65, D&A15. No other operating items.

[Channel KPI policy] Merchandise gross margin excludes selling/fulfillment. Marketplace contribution=commission minus marketplace operating cost. Total GMV=sum own net sales and marketplace GMV, not recognized revenue.
[Orders] Online own business 3 million orders, marketplace 4 million orders. Return count not disclosed. Own online net sales after returns; marketplace GMV net of returns.
[Cash] Audited CFO38 and cash capex22. Marketplace customer cash gross300 and seller settlements separately reflected in CFO. No opening seller payable or timing details.
[Management deck] Calls 950 GMV 'total revenue'; divides store and online GP plus marketplace commission by GMV as recognized gross margin. Attributes online growth exclusively to more orders.
[Prior period KPI note] 2024 online order count unavailable. No independent cohort or customer acquisition data. No future store closure plan.

qas.question: Find FY2025 own-store recognized net revenue.
Find total recognized group revenue, respecting the marketplace agent policy.
Find FY2025 total GMV under the stated definition.
Find reported revenue growth against the prior audited recognized revenue.
Find own-store merchandise gross margin on its net sales.
Find own-online merchandise gross profit before fulfillment.
Find marketplace contribution under the channel metric.
Calculate group EBITDA from disclosed channel and corporate costs.
Find the recognized group operating profit after D&A.
Find own-online net revenue per order in dollars.
Find FCF using audited CFO and cash capital spending.
Explain why 950m should not be labeled recognized revenue.
qas.answer: It includes the entire 300m third-party marketplace GMV. The group earns 36m commission as agent; recognized revenue is686m, not950m.

qas.question: Can the blended merchandise gross margin be obtained by dividing channel contribution by total GMV?
qas.answer: No. The denominator includes seller transaction value and the numerator mixes gross profit and commission; use a consistently defined recognized-revenue or GMV metric.

qas.question: Can 2025 online order growth be measured from current three million orders?
qas.answer: No. The prior-year order count is missing. Revenue growth alone mixes volume, price and mix.

qas.question: Can the exact year-end seller payable be reconstructed from GMV300 and commission36?
qas.answer: No. Opening liability, settlements, adjustments and timing are missing.

qas.question: Does a higher online sales share establish lower total customer acquisition cost?
qas.answer: No. Marketing, customer cohorts, attribution and repeat orders are not disclosed.

assumptions: USD million. Fictional Golden Fern Insurance. Toy final accounts gross reserve and recovery assets separate. Counterparty exposure measured on gross recognized recoverables; collateral reduces exposure analytically only when explicitly eligible. No assumed legal offset.

evidence.text: [Reserve note] Gross unpaid claims reserve600, reinsurance recoverable180. Gross reserve comprises current AY220 and prior AY380. Ceded recoverables include paid-claim receivables50 and unpaid-claim recovery estimate130.

[Counterparty table]
|Reinsurer|Recognized recoverable|Eligible collateral|Disputed extra unrecognized claim|
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|A|90|30|20|
|B|60|10|0|
|C|30|0|15|

[Credit policy] Eligible collateral may reduce analytical unsecured exposure; recognized recoverables remain gross before allowance. Approved ECL rates on unsecured exposures A2%, B5%, C10%. No existing allowance; recognized ECL expense equals computed charge.

[P&L] Net earned premium500, net incurred claims330 before reinsurance credit impairment, underwriting expense110. Reinsurance credit impairment outside combined ratio by stated definition, but reduces total operating result. Investment net income25, tax10, no other items.
[Capital] Eligible capital before this newly calculated ECL charge250; required capital200. No tax adjustment to the ECL charge in capital bridge.
[Risk scenario] A eligible collateral loses 50% of value; A ECL rate rises to8%, other counterparties unchanged. Recompute total ECL, do not add entire stress allowance on top of base charge.

[Presentation] CFO subtracts collateral40 and disputed extra35 from gross recoverables; calls net reserve420 after offset a legal liability. Claims all disputed claims will be recovered because treaty exists.
[Audit instruction] No legal offset right, recovery cash schedule, reinsurer default correlations or actual litigation outcomes. All stress numbers hypothetical.

qas.question: Find total recognized recoverables from the counterparty table.
Find recognized recoverables as share of gross unpaid claims; identify the scope mismatch.
qas.answer: 180/600=30%; this mixes paid receivables50 with unpaid recoveries130, so not a pure unpaid reserve cession ratio.

qas.question: Find unpaid-claim recovery estimate as share of gross unpaid reserve.
Find A's base unsecured exposure after eligible collateral.
Find total base analytical unsecured exposure.
Calculate approved ECL charge on the three unsecured exposures.
Find net carrying recoverable after ECL, without netting collateral.
Calculate underwriting combined ratio before excluded counterparty impairment.
Find net income after newly recognized reinsurance credit impairment.
Find base eligible capital ratio after ECL charge.
Find stressed ECL charge after A's collateral haircut and increased rate.
Find incremental ECL increase from base to stress.
Why is 600−180=420 not the recognized gross claims liability?
qas.answer: Recoverables are separate assets, and 50 relates to paid claims; no legal offset is allowed. Gross liability remains600.

qas.question: Should the 35 disputed extra claims reduce recognized exposure or be included as assured recoveries?
qas.answer: No. They are unrecognized and disputed; no acceptance or outcome supports either adjustment.

qas.question: Can collateral be deducted twice, from carrying recoverable and again from ECL exposure?
qas.answer: No. The toy uses collateral only in analytical exposure for ECL; gross carrying recoverable180 less ECL is separate.

qas.question: Can the probability of simultaneous reinsurer failures be calculated?
qas.answer: No. Rates here determine toy ECL, not joint default distribution; correlations and default/recovery data are absent.

assumptions: USD million. Fictional Amber Courtyard REIT. Toy property fair value changes through P&L, FFO excludes property disposal gain and fair value gain, no depreciation in fair-value property model. AFFO subtracts maintenance capex and straight-line rent adjustment.

evidence.text: [Opening balance] Investment properties800, cash50, other assets20, gross debt400, other liabilities70. Common equity400. No preferred/NCI.

[Property movements] Cash acquisition100 at Jan1; cash improvements30 capitalized. Property sold with carrying80 for proceeds95, no selling cost. Year-end valuation gain50 on remaining properties. No other property movements.
[P&L] Rental revenue120 includes straight-line rent accrual8 above cash billings. Property expense45, central expense15, interest25, tax5. Gain on property sale and fair value gain separate; no D&A.

[Cash] Rental cash collections105, property expense cash43, central expense15, interest25, tax5. CFO17. Improvements30 comprise maintenance10, expansion20. Acquisition100, sale proceeds95; net new borrowing60, dividend20. No other cash movement.
[Metric] FFO=net profit less fair-value gain and sale gain. AFFO=FFO minus maintenance capex and straight-line rent accrual8. Net debt uses unrestricted cash; restricted cash10 at year-end.
[Capital] Closing gross debt460; year-end common units50m. Property valuation is appraisal, no sale commitment. Other assets/liabilities at closing not specified.
[Presentation] Sponsor says net profit includes only rental operations and fair value gain50 provides cash for distributions. Uses total capital improvements30 as maintenance in AFFO.
[Audit note] Future rent, financing and sale proceeds uncertain. No market price per unit.

qas.question: Find gain on the property disposed of during the year.
Find closing investment property carrying value after all movements.
Find rental NOI before corporate expense.
Find reported profit after tax, including valuation and sale gains.
Find FFO under the specified REIT definition.
Find AFFO after maintenance capex and straight-line rent adjustment.
Find AFFO per common unit.
Find total closing cash from the stated cash flow.
Find closing covenant net debt using unrestricted cash only.
Find dividend payout ratio relative to AFFO in the toy.
Why is fair-value gain not cash available for dividends?
qas.answer: It is a noncash carrying adjustment. Actual collections, cash expense, investment and debt flows determine liquidity.

qas.question: Why does the 95m sale receipt not equal the 15m gain?
qas.answer: Cash proceeds must be compared with 80m carrying value to determine gain; the remaining 80m is recovery of asset carrying value.

qas.question: Is the stated AFFO calculated by deducting all 30 improvements?
qas.answer: No. The definition deducts maintenance10 only, plus straight-line accrual8. Expansion20 is separate capital spending and still uses cash.

qas.question: Can total closing common NAV per unit be found from property900 and debt460 alone?
qas.answer: No. Need closing other assets, liabilities and all equity claims. Opening balances cannot be silently carried forward.

qas.question: Can the future dividend be guaranteed from accounting profit95?
qas.answer: No. AFFO12, actual cash needs, debt maturities and distribution policy differ from accounting profit; no binding future dividend.

qas.question: Can the market discount to NAV be determined?
qas.answer: No. Market unit price and full current NAV are not supplied.

assumptions: USD million. Fictional Cedar Atlas private fund. Toy fund reporting distinguishes cash realization, residual fair-value NAV and external capital calls. Multiples defined on paid-in capital; no leverage/tax outside stated expenses.

evidence.text: [Opening register] Cumulative paid-in capital120, cumulative distributions20, opening residual NAV110. No other capital commitments counted as paid-in.
[Current capital calls] Investors contribute30 cash this year. Uncalled commitments70 remain. Fund invests new cash40, no return of capital to investor until actual distribution.
[Investment events] Holding A disposed: carrying25, proceeds40. Remaining holdings fair-value gain18, no other investment gain. Portfolio interest income5 cash; fund fees8 cash. No other expenses.
[Cash/distribution] Current investor distribution25 paid in cash. Opening cash10. Capital calls30, sale proceeds40 and interest5 received, new investments40, fees8, distributions25 paid. No debt.

[Metrics] DPI=cumulative distributions / paid-in capital. RVPI=residual NAV / paid-in capital. TVPI=(distributions+residual NAV)/paid-in capital. Net NAV bridge includes capital calls, distributions and current net P&L. Multiples use actual paid-in, not commitments.
[Reporting] Latest signed valuation committee marks remaining assets as given. Indicative buyer offer for one holding10% above valuation is nonbinding, no adjustment approved.
[Deck] Reports TVPI using paid-in plus uncalled commitments denominator and labels residual NAV as cash returned; also includes sale proceeds40 as full gain.
[Limitations] No dated investor flows beyond this year's aggregates, no benchmark, no final exit or individual tax information.

qas.question: Find recognized gain on sale of holding A.
Find current total net investment P&L after fees.
Find cumulative paid-in capital at year-end.
Find cumulative distributions paid to investors.
Reconcile ending residual NAV after external flows and net result.
Find DPI at year-end under the stated definition.
Find RVPI on residual NAV.
Find TVPI from cumulative realized and residual value.
Reconcile closing actual cash from the cash ledger.
Find proportion of total measured investor value already distributed.
Why do uncalled commitments70 not increase the paid-in denominator?
qas.answer: They are future funding obligations not yet paid. The metric expressly uses capital actually called and received.

qas.question: Why is residual NAV145 not cash returned to investors?
qas.answer: It includes remaining investments at valuation and cash still inside the fund. Cash distributions are cumulative45; residual NAV may not realize at carrying value.

qas.question: Should the nonbinding buyer offer change reported residual NAV automatically?
qas.answer: No. The final approved valuation controls; the offer is indicative and not an approved mark or binding sale.

qas.question: Can an exact net IRR be calculated from TVPI and DPI?
qas.answer: No. IRR requires dated capital calls and distributions, not just aggregate multiples and current NAV.

qas.question: Can the gain on disposal be increased by including the 40 cash proceeds as additional profit?
qas.answer: No. Gain is already proceeds minus carrying (15); treating proceeds as profit double-counts carrying recovery.

qas.question: Can the future final TVPI be guaranteed above 1.26x?
qas.answer: No. Residual value, later expenses, remaining capital calls and final exit proceeds can change.
